<h1 id="Paper-011-%E2%80%94-Counterdiabatic-Driving-of-Evolution">Paper 011 — Counterdiabatic Driving of Evolution<a class="anchor-link" href="#Paper-011-%E2%80%94-Counterdiabatic-Driving-of-Evolution">¶</a></h1><p><strong>Iram, Dolson, Chiel, Hu, Nicholson, Ponce, Butts, Raman, Ohno (2020).</strong> <a href="https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-020-0989-3"><em>Controlling the speed and trajectory of evolution with counterdiabatic driving</em></a>. <em>Nature Physics</em> <strong>17</strong>, 135–142. <a href="https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-020-0989-3">doi:10.1038/s41567-020-0989-3</a></p>
<p>This paper externally validates that evolution can be controlled — steered along specific trajectories at specified speeds — using counterdiabatic driving from quantum thermodynamics. We reproduce the Wright-Fisher population dynamics on NK fitness landscapes with naive vs counterdiabatic (CD) drug schedules.</p>
<p>Adapted from <code>control/counterdiabatic/counterdiabatic_evolution.py</code>.</p>
<p><strong>Provenance:</strong> <code>src/provenance/experiments.rs</code> — <code>COUNTERDIABATIC_PROVENANCE</code>.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="Background">Background<a class="anchor-link" href="#Background">¶</a></h2><ul>
<li><p><strong>NK fitness landscapes.</strong> Each genotype has $N$ binary loci with <strong>K</strong> epistatic interactions: each locus’s fitness contribution depends on its own allele and $K$ other loci’ states. Total fitness averages per-locus contributions; ruggedness rises with <strong>K</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li><p><strong>Wright–Fisher population dynamics.</strong> Generations follow fitness-based selection then multinomial resampling at fixed census. The deterministic (mean-field) limit corresponds to infinite population size and matches the regime where CD theory is exact here.</p>
</li>
<li><p><strong>Drug concentration schedule.</strong> A parameter $s(t) \in [0,1]$ mixes two landscapes: drug-absent $\mathbf{F}_0$ and drug-present $\mathbf{F}_1$, via $\mathbf{F}_s = (1-s)\mathbf{F}_0 + s \mathbf{F}_1$.</p>
</li>
<li><p><strong>Counterdiabatic protocol.</strong> CD scheduling uses the <strong>Fisher information metric</strong> along $s$: more protocol time where Boltzmann-weighted fitness variance is high (“transitions”), less where it is flat.</p>
</li>
<li><p><strong>BarraCUDA connection.</strong> Alignment with kernels: <code>gemm_f64.wgsl</code> for batch fitness, <code>softmax.wgsl</code> for Boltzmann weights, and reductions for Fisher-information aggregates.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing code_cell rendered">
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="NK-Fitness-Landscape">NK Fitness Landscape<a class="anchor-link" href="#NK-Fitness-Landscape">¶</a></h2><p>Following Kauffman–Levin NK models, genotypes are binary strings of length <strong>N</strong>. Each locus $i$ contributes a value read from a lookup table indexed by $\{i\}$ and <strong>K</strong> distinct neighbor loci, so epistasis couples each site to $K+1$ bits total. <strong>Fitness</strong> is the mean of the $N$ contributions. Here $2^N$ is small ($N=5$), so we can enumerate all genotypes and evaluate full-landscape vectors.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing code_cell rendered">
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="Wright-Fisher-Population-Dynamics">Wright-Fisher Population Dynamics<a class="anchor-link" href="#Wright-Fisher-Population-Dynamics">¶</a></h2><p>We use Boltzmann equilibrium weights, interpolated fitness $\mathbf{F}_s$, and the <strong>deterministic Wright–Fisher</strong> update (frequency reweighting without multinomial noise). <code>run_protocol_deterministic</code> marches $\mathbf{p}_t$ along the schedule and records $\mathrm{KL}(\mathbf{p}_t \,\|\, \boldsymbol{\pi}_s)$ versus the instantaneous equilibrium $\boldsymbol{\pi}_s$.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing code_cell rendered">
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="Counterdiabatic-Schedule">Counterdiabatic Schedule<a class="anchor-link" href="#Counterdiabatic-Schedule">¶</a></h2><p><code>compute_cd_schedule</code> builds $s^{*}(t)$ from $\sqrt{g(s)}$ with $g(s) \approx \beta^2 \mathrm{Var}_s[F]$ under interpolated fitness, normalizing cumulative “thermodynamic arclength.” The schedule slows where information geometry is stiff and speeds up where it is flat.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing code_cell rendered">
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="Validation:-NK-Landscape-Construction">Validation: NK Landscape Construction<a class="anchor-link" href="#Validation:-NK-Landscape-Construction">¶</a></h2><p>We instantiate two independent landscapes per $K$: <strong>F₀</strong> (seed 42) and <strong>F₁</strong> (seed 99), both with $N=5$. Correlation between <strong>F₀</strong> and <strong>F₁</strong> is reported for context; the interpolation $s(t)$ will drive the population from equilibrium under <strong>F₀</strong> toward the target equilibrium under <strong>F₁</strong>.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<p>This notebook executes <strong>Parts 1–4</strong> explicitly; for Parts <strong>5–7</strong>, run <strong><code>main()</code></strong> in <code>control/counterdiabatic/counterdiabatic_evolution.py</code>.</p>
<h3 id="Key-findings">Key findings<a class="anchor-link" href="#Key-findings">¶</a></h3><ul>
<li><strong>Counterdiabatic driving on NK landscapes</strong> reduces final $\ell_1$ distance to the target distribution versus a naive linear ramp in $s(t)$.</li>
<li><strong>Adiabaticity:</strong> trajectory-averaged KL from instantaneous equilibrium favors CD.</li>
<li><strong>Non-uniform schedules:</strong> time allocation from the Fisher-information construction is central—analogous in spirit to adaptive learning-rate curricula in optimization.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="ecoPrimals-connection">ecoPrimals connection<a class="anchor-link" href="#ecoPrimals-connection">¶</a></h3><ul>
<li>Drug schedule $\rightarrow$ <strong>primal constraint</strong> schedule</li>
<li>NK landscape $\rightarrow$ <strong>loss landscape</strong></li>
<li>Wright–Fisher $\rightarrow$ <strong>SGD with noise</strong> (stochastic finite population) / mean-field selection (deterministic cells above)</li>
<li>CD protocol $\rightarrow$ <strong>scheduled control</strong>, comparable in role to LR scheduling</li>
</ul>
